about_p1: Pakarina is an interdisciplinary technological initiative focused on supporting dengue monitoring, prevention, analysis, and awareness activities through the development of a centralized digital platform. The project was created with the objective of bringing together information, tools, devices, and people that currently operate in separate environments, allowing more efficient coordination between technical teams, researchers, educators, and institutions involved in public health and environmental monitoring activities.
about_p2: The name Pakarina represents a collaborative effort where technology becomes a bridge between data collection, analysis, education, and community action. The project combines software engineering, hardware integration, data management, educational outreach, and organizational coordination into a single ecosystem designed to support informed decision-making and continuous improvement.
about_p3: At its core, Pakarina is developing a modern web platform capable of integrating information from sensors, monitoring devices, databases, mapping systems, external services, and educational resources. Instead of maintaining isolated systems and disconnected workflows, the platform seeks to create a unified environment where relevant information can be collected, processed, visualized, and managed through a single access point. This approach improves traceability, reduces fragmentation, and facilitates collaboration among all participating areas.
about_p4: The platform is designed as a scalable and adaptable foundation that can evolve over time. Its architecture supports the integration of hardware devices, environmental monitoring equipment, centralized data storage, visualization dashboards, user and access management mechanisms, geographic information systems, external APIs, and operational tools that support both technical and educational activities.
about_p5: Pakarina is much more than a software project. It is organized as a multidisciplinary collaboration involving professionals and contributors from different areas, including project management, software development, hardware and infrastructure integration, user experience design, educational outreach, awareness campaigns, operational support, and academic collaboration. Each area contributes unique expertise while working toward a shared objective: creating a technological ecosystem capable of supporting dengue-related initiatives through innovation, coordination, and knowledge sharing.
about_p6: Beyond its operational objectives, Pakarina also contributes to academic and methodological development. The project serves as a practical environment where interdisciplinary collaboration, adaptive management approaches, organizational coordination mechanisms, and technology integration strategies can be observed and analyzed. This creates opportunities to generate valuable knowledge regarding how complex technological initiatives can be managed in dynamic and evolving environments while maintaining their practical impact and institutional independence.
about_p7: Our vision is to build a sustainable technological ecosystem that strengthens monitoring capabilities, improves information accessibility, supports educational initiatives, and promotes collaboration between technical and non-technical participants. By combining technology, research, community engagement, and interdisciplinary teamwork, Pakarina seeks to create tools and knowledge that contribute not only to operational efficiency but also to broader efforts related to public health, environmental awareness, and innovation-driven problem solving.
about_p8: Through collaboration, adaptability, and continuous improvement, Pakarina aims to demonstrate how technology can be transformed into a practical instrument for connecting people, information, and action in pursuit of meaningful and lasting impact.
contact_intro: Pakarina is a collaborative initiative developed by the Federal University of Ouro Preto (UFOP) in partnership with the Catholic University of Salta (UCASAL) and Yncrea.
